title: inputmode, enterkeyhint, placeholder limitations
learningObjectives: Explain inputmode, enterkeyhint, placeholder limitations and build forms with appropriate native HTML behaviour.

understand.concept: inputmode hints which virtual keyboard layout may be useful, while enterkeyhint suggests the label or action for the virtual keyboard's Enter key. placeholder provides a short example or hint inside an empty control, but it is not a substitute for a persistent label or instructions.
understand.whyItMatters: Mobile input hints improve data entry but do not validate the value. Placeholder text disappears as users type and may have insufficient contrast, so keep visible labels and instructions.
understand.analogy: inputmode chooses a keyboard suggestion; placeholder is a temporary hint written inside the field, not its name.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual form submission and validation follow HTML algorithms and browser behaviour.

explain.narrative: The field has a visible label and supporting instructions. inputmode and enterkeyhint influence the virtual keyboard but do not validate the input.

examples.code: <form><label for='pin'>One-time code</label><input id='pin' name='pin' inputmode='numeric' enterkeyhint='done' placeholder='6-digit code' aria-describedby='pin-help'><small id='pin-help'>Enter the code sent to you.</small></form>
examples.explanation: The field has a visible label and supporting instructions. inputmode and enterkeyhint influence the virtual keyboard but do not validate the input.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered form demonstrating the HTML form behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Create a mobile-friendly form with numeric and email input hints. Remove the placeholder and confirm the field remains understandable because its label and instructions are present.
practise.independentTask: Build an accessible form using appropriate input types, names, labels, and constraints. Inspect the submitted FormData and explain which controls are successful.
hints: Give every user-facing control a visible label.
Do not trust hidden fields or client-side validation for security.
Test keyboard and mobile input behaviour.

questions.prompt: Can placeholder replace a visible form label?
questions.explanation: Placeholder is a hint and disappears; it does not replace a persistent label.

questions.prompt: What is a good form-design principle?
options: Use semantic controls, visible labels, and server-side validation
questions.answer: Use semantic controls, visible labels, and server-side validation
questions.explanation: Accessible forms use appropriate controls and labels, while security validation belongs on the server.
